root_motivation: WHO: an agent reading host.table.query, host.runs.list or host.docs.list on a plan or client that cannot use a very large answer, and Joe, who sets the byte budget by editing one plan row. WHAT: nothing sizes a page of a paged verb and nothing tells an agent where a shorter page stopped, so a client that cuts the text on its side reasons over a partial result as if it were whole. WHY: a page over the plan's byte budget must be cut at a row boundary and name its size, the full size and the exact next call, and a cut must never happen without that marker.
user_persona: An agent (or its operator) paging a host list verb or a SQL result who needs every page to fit a stated budget, end on a whole row, and carry a continue_with call it can make verbatim; and an operator who raises the pro budget by editing one plan row.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a page cut for budget on a paged verb, When rszb_ac01_one_truncation_struct serializes _meta.mcphost.truncated, Then it has exactly the keys bytes, of and continue_with, and a response that was also clamped by limit holds both limit_clamped and truncated under _meta.mcphost.

Given each verb in PAGED_VERBS with enough rows to pass an 8 KiB plan budget, When it is read at its maximum limit and every continue_with is followed verbatim, Then each page is within 8 KiB or is one row, ends on a whole row, continue_with.args.limit equals the request's limit, and the walk visits every row once; Given host.channel.read {ack: true} cut, Then the stored position is the last row kept.

Given the free and pro plans, When host.quickstart runs, Then limits.plan.response_budget_bytes equals the plan struct's field, limits.output_bytes_max still reads the 1 MiB wall, and render_ceilings_table lists the field in docs/plans.md with the docs drift test green.

Given a python tool that returns a 2 MiB line, When called synchronously, Then the existing tool_output_too_large answers with limit_bytes equal to limits.output_bytes_max and no truncated key; Given a non-paged verb under the wall, Then its response is whole.

Given a 5 MiB table and a 32 KiB plan budget, When host.table.query {sql: "SELECT * FROM t", limit: 1000} runs and each continue_with is followed, Then every page is within the budget and ends on a whole row and the walk visits every row once; Given an empty table, Then rows: [] with no marker.

Given prod after landing, When tests/rszb_ac06_live_prod_quickstart_budget.rs calls anonymous host.quickstart {}, Then limits.plan.response_budget_bytes is a positive integer (Live; evidence: MCPHOST_LIVE=1 MCPHOST_URL=https://mcphost.dev cargo test --test rszb_ac06_live_prod_quickstart_budget)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: Live (prod; evidence: MCPHOST_LIVE=1 MCPHOST_URL=https://mcphost.dev cargo test --test rszb_ac06_live_prod_quickstart_budget)

scope: src/response_budget.rs (Truncated, Call, cut_page, cut_values, budget_of); src/plans.rs (response_budget_bytes); src/paged.rs (project_rows); the byte-budget cut in src/runs.rs, src/docs.rs, src/calllog.rs, src/messaging.rs and src/channels.rs; src/tables.rs and src/handler/arms.rs (host.table.query offset and cut); src/handler.rs (_meta.mcphost.truncated, host.table.query descriptor); docs/plans.md, docs/tools.md, docs/openapi.json, contracts/host-tools.v1.json and the SDKs rendered from it.
non_goals: A per-client budget axis; compression; streaming; cutting a non-paged response; paging host.tool.logs; the AC 6 prod read (operator-provisioned, deferred).

additional.no_version_bump: No version file is bumped; wm-build land bumps and tags.
additional.one_marker: A cut is reported only as _meta.mcphost.truncated {bytes, of, continue_with}; the kinds' 1 MiB wall still refuses and never cuts.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can an agent reason over a partial result as if it were whole?
five_whys_trace.a: A page of a paged verb has no byte bound and nothing says where a shorter page stopped.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is there no byte bound?
five_whys_trace.a: limits.output_bytes_max is one global 1 MiB constant read only by the kinds; the plan catalog has no byte ceiling.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not cut at the wall?
five_whys_trace.a: The wall refuses a synchronous kind call and chunks an async run; a cut is only well defined at a row boundary of a paged verb.

five_whys_trace.q: Why must the cut carry a continue_with?
five_whys_trace.a: A cut without the next call is worse than an error; the keyset cursor each verb already mints makes the call exact.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does host.table.query need an offset?
five_whys_trace.a: It has limit but no continuation, so its cut page could not be resumed without the agent rewriting its own SQL.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where is the size measured, before or after fields projection?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: After: the page is projected first and the serialized rows array is what is compared with the budget, so bytes and of equal what the client receives.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What does a row larger than the whole budget do?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: It is returned alone (a page always keeps at least one row), and the next continue_with resumes after it.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Offset or keyset for host.table.query?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Offset, applied as LIMIT n OFFSET m over the caller's own SELECT, because arbitrary SELECTs, row-policy rewrites and CTEs do not guarantee a rowid order.
